notes: Credential-eligibility page. ETCP explicitly targets experienced riggers and maintains separate Arena and Theatre credentials. This supports an external specialist gate rather than a novice online qualification path.

jurisdiction_scope: ETCP Arena Rigger body of knowledge

title: 29 CFR 1910.28 — Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where Subpart D applies; exceptions and other standards may control specific work
role_scope: employees exposed to covered fall/falling-object hazards
notes: Use only for applicable fall/falling-object authority claims. The rule contains scope exceptions, including an entertainment-stage perimeter exception, so it must not be generalized into one universal rigging fall rule.

title: 29 CFR 1910.29 — Fall protection systems and falling object protection — criteria and practices
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where Subpart D applies
notes: Criteria source only. Crew Blueprint general courses should not convert criteria into work-at-height procedure or equipment-selection instruction.

jurisdiction_scope: voluntary consensus standard unless adopted/required by contract, venue, code or authority
model_product_scope: permanently installed manually operated counterweight rigging systems
notes: Publisher-index metadata for ANSI E1.4-1-2022 scope/version. Full standard text should be used where a final claim depends on its detailed requirements.

title: ANSI E1.6-3 — 2019 Selection and Use of Serially Manufactured Chain Hoists in the Entertainment Industry
jurisdiction_scope: voluntary consensus standard unless adopted/required by contract, venue, code or authority

notes: Publisher-index metadata for ANSI E1.6-3-2019 scope/version. Detailed operational requirements require the controlling standard text and specialist review.

title: Fall protection for the entertainment industry under the OSH Act of 1970
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry (29 CFR 1910, Subparts D and I) applied to entertainment-industry fall hazards
role_scope: riggers and technicians working at height in entertainment venues
freshness_trigger: OSHA reissues or withdraws this interpretation, or 1910.28/1910.29 amendment changes its premise
notes: On-point primary confirmation that OSHA treats entertainment rigging/technician work as general industry (1910), not construction (1926) — 'OSHA does not have any industry specific standards for the entertainment industry.' States a climbing belt/Swiss seat is a positioning device only, not fall protection; a full body harness is required for fall protection at height. Predates 1910.28's 2016 walking-working-surfaces rewrite, so cross-check against current 1910.28 text (S-OSHA-1910-28-CURRENT) rather than relying on this letter alone for the exact current stage-perimeter exception boundary.

title: 29 CFR 1910.184 — Slings
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry material handling by hoisting
model_product_scope: alloy steel chain, wire rope, metal mesh, natural/synthetic fiber rope, and synthetic web slings
role_scope: anyone handling, inspecting, or working near rigging slings
notes: Real general-industry (not construction-only) authority for sling rejection criteria: damage/defects, wear beyond manufacturer spec, deformation/kinking, heat damage/corrosion, cracked or bent hooks, missing identification tags, shock-loading prohibition, and the requirement that a competent person designated by the employer performs the formal daily inspection. Directly supports a ground-rigger 'recognize and report' lesson without granting inspection-sign-off authority, which stays with the employer-designated competent person.
